research_progress.source_confidence_semantics: Heuristic research-source confidence only. Direct official GOV.UK, Defra UK-AIR, UKHSA, Planning Data and London City Hall pages checked on 25 July 2026. AQMA boundaries, national monitoring statistics, PM2.5 targets, heat-health alerts, adopted London guidance and draft 2026 London Plan material remain at their published geographic and temporal scope. They are not parcel-level pollutant measurements, health predictions, planning outcomes, heat models or Future Growth score accuracy.

source_facts.fact: Planning Data reports 498 Air Quality Management Areas; collector last ran 24 July 2026 and origin is authoritative.
source_facts.gate: AQMA intersection is planning-screening evidence, not a parcel pollutant concentration or refusal.

source_facts.fact: England's 2040 PM2.5 targets are 10 micrograms per cubic metre annual mean or lower and at least 35% population-exposure reduction from 2018; 2025 population exposure was 26% below 2018.
source_facts.gate: National monitoring-target progress must not be downscaled into a parcel air-quality value.

source_facts.fact: In 2025, 97% of 111 qualifying AURN stations in England were at or below 10 micrograms per cubic metre; the highest measured annual mean was 12.
source_facts.gate: Monitoring-station statistics do not establish an unmonitored site's concentration.

source_facts.fact: The 13 July 2026 update described yellow alerts for seven English regions for 14 to 17 July 2026.
source_facts.gate: An expired regional alert must not be represented as a current or parcel-specific heat-risk state on 25 July 2026.

source_facts.fact: Air Quality Neutral and Air Quality Positive London Plan Guidance are adopted guidance from 8 February 2023.
source_facts.gate: Adopted guidance is a planning consideration and methodology, not proof that a particular scheme complies.

source_facts.fact: The greener, healthier and resilient city chapter is explicitly Draft London Plan material published 16 July 2026.
source_facts.gate: Draft 2026 policy must not be represented as adopted London Plan policy.

core_rules: AQMA designation is not a parcel pollutant measurement
AQMA intersection does not automatically make development unacceptable
absence of AQMA intersection does not prove clean air at a parcel
AQMA boundaries and revocations must be date-versioned
national air-quality targets are not parcel thresholds for automatic scoring
AURN station readings must not be copied to an unmonitored parcel
monitoring-station distance alone does not justify concentration interpolation
annual mean concentration is not a short-term peak concentration
population exposure indicator is not an individual exposure estimate
PERT progress is not a local authority compliance score
PM2.5 target progress must retain the qualifying-station methodology
data-capture thresholds must not be ignored when using monitoring statistics
2025 national statistics must not be relabelled as 2026 parcel measurements
emissions inventory trends are not ambient concentration measurements
UK-wide pollutant statistics must not be downscaled without a supported method
damage costs are appraisal values and not parcel remediation costs
damage-cost guidance does not establish planning permission outcome
Clean Air Strategy policy is not site-specific compliance evidence
local authority action-plan status is not proof a parcel breaches an objective
LAQM annual review obligations are not development refusal rules
PM2.5 planning guidance requires consideration but does not itself calculate site impact
ambient-air targets apply broadly but parcel impacts require project-specific evidence
regional heat-health alerts are not permanent heat-risk classifications
expired heat-health alerts must not be shown as current alerts
heat-health alert level is not a parcel overheating model
health alert geography is not cadastral geometry
weather-health alerts do not substitute for building overheating assessment
UK climate-risk assessment is strategic evidence not a parcel forecast
national climate risks must not be converted into parcel probabilities
London Plan 2021 adopted policy must remain distinct from Draft London Plan 2026
draft London policy must not be represented as current adopted policy
Air Quality Neutral guidance is methodology not automatic scheme compliance
Air Quality Positive guidance applies by scope and is not a universal parcel score
Air Quality Positive statement requirement is not planning approval
UGF is a proposal-design tool and not existing parcel ecological condition
UGF targets must not be calculated without scheme surface-cover inputs
urban greening does not erase air-quality or heat constraints
London strategic policy must not be applied outside its jurisdiction
London citywide emissions context is not a parcel emission inventory
NOx and particulate benchmarks must remain pollutant-specific
construction air impacts are distinct from completed-development benchmarks
transport emissions and building emissions must not be conflated
current pollution forecast is not an annual planning baseline
historic pollution reports are not current real-time measurements
official statistical confidence does not equal parcel-level accuracy
screening evidence must remain separate from business promotion
NO_DATA for parcel concentration must not be converted into no-risk
no parcel relation or Future Growth score may be emitted while recovery is parked
